$comment: Mission 1.70 §18 to §22. Documentation only. No BigQuery was executed and no HAR was fetched.

source_says: Crawl dates are always rounded down to the first of the month, regardless of which day they actually started.
the June 2023 crawl kicks off on the 13th of the month, but the dataset would be accessible on BigQuery under the date `2023-06-01`
run_identity.immutability_reason: a run is addressable by its rounded date; no retrieved page states that a published run remains available unchanged

source_says: The URLs come from the Chrome User Experience Report, a dataset of real user performance data of the most popular websites.
one row per page tested in the HTTP Archive. Pages are tested on a monthly basis
population_identity.attempted_set_reason: the page metadata blob carries retry_count, tested_url and visited, which are attempt-level facts. Whether a page whose test never succeeded appears at all is not stated.
population_identity.failed_tests_reason: the pages table carries no column for a failed, errored or unusable test, and no retrieved page states whether such a page yields a row
population_identity.operator_frozen_reason: the population is defined by a third party's telemetry of what Chrome users visit, and cannot be replaced by a corpus we choose

source_says: date: YYYY-MM-DD format of the HTTP Archive monthly crawl
page: The URL of the page being tested
rank: Site popularity rank, from CrUX
tested_url: actual URL of the page that was intended to be tested
visited: Array of URLs visited during test
page_metadata_blob.project_interpretation: retry_count, tested_url and visited are genuine attempt-level metadata and are more than Common Crawl publishes. What is still missing is a status for the test itself.

response_availability.$comment: §20. Mission 1.69 left this open and it is now answered.
source_says: one row per request per page tested in the HTTP Archive

redirects.source_says: is_main_document: Whether this request corresponds with the main HTML document of the page, which is the first HTML request after redirects
redirects.initial_versus_final_response: the main document is identified as the first HTML request AFTER redirects, so the row a predicate would naturally bind to is the POST-redirect document
redirects.row_identity: page is the URL of the page being tested and url is the URL of the request; tested_url records the URL intended to be tested, which the documentation notes is useful where redirects create ambiguity

browser_semantics.$comment: §22. Not the same act as a crawler fetch, and saying so is the point.
browser_semantics.execution_apparatus: a private instance of WebPageTest with private test agents that are real browsers
source_says: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 8.1.0; Moto G (4))...Chrome/138.0.0.0 Mobile Safari
Google Cloud Platform locations based in the USA
All pages are tested with an empty cache in a logged out state, which may not reflect how real users would access them.
a home page is not necessarily representative of the entire website

route_status_reason: Structured response headers, text bodies, dated addressable runs, attempt-level metadata and an unusually complete request contract are established. What is not established is whether failed tests are represented, how intermediate redirect hops appear, and the data licence.
